artworks.title: The Erinyes Drive Alcmaeon from the Corpse of Eriphyle
artworks.description: Kunsthaus Zürich: Fuseli seizes the Epigoni captain's aftermath — Alcmaeon flees Eriphyle's corpse as the Erinyes swarm, the necklace-revenge that avenges Amphiaraus and pollutes the second Theban war's leader.

artworks.title: Alcmaeon Killing His Mother Eriphyle
artworks.description: Pompeian fresco (Naples): Alcmaeon strikes down the mother who sold Amphiaraus into the Seven — the matricide that binds the Epigoni generation to Orestes' kind of pollution.

artworks.title: Eriphyle Suckling Alcmaeon, with Amphiaraus
artworks.description: Attic hydria: Amphiaraus leans on his staff while Eriphyle suckles infant Alcmaeon — domestic calm before the necklace, the Seven's failure, and the sons' return.

artworks.title: The Erinyes beside the Body of Eriphyle
artworks.description: Fuseli's pendant treatment: the Furies crowd Eriphyle's corpse as Alcmaeon is driven into exile — Romantic tragedy fixing the Epigoni matricide as the cycle's second Orestes.

popCulture.title: Epigoni (epic)
popCulture.description: The lost cyclic sequel to the Thebaid — the sons of the Seven take Thebes at last, and only a line or two of the old poem survives.

popCulture.title: Epigoni
popCulture.description: Alcmaeon, Diomedes, and the second Argive generation — the revenge war that closes the Theban cycle before Troy.

popCulture.title: Theban Cycle
popCulture.description: The Epigoni sit in the cycle between the Seven's failure and the Trojan generation — Cadmus' city falling twice in epic memory.

popCulture.title: Thebaid
popCulture.creator: Statius
popCulture.description: Statius' Latin epic ends with the Seven, but its Theban war remains the chief surviving frame for every later Epigoni retelling.
